rationale: Direct-match cluster is the two Alcohol use disorder models (PGS002738, PGS002739); the two “Problematic alcohol use” scores (PGS000201, PGS000202) are a weaker endpoint match (measurement/count phenotype) and show small ΔR², so they are less likely to top an alcohol-dependence benchmark. Between the two AUD candidates, PGS002738 has stronger visible discriminative evidence (OR top 10% vs rest 1.96 vs 1.76 for PGS002739) and uses a standard genome-wide PRS-CS with far broader variant coverage (326k vs 858), which is a favorable structural signal for a polygenic endpoint when AUC/R² are missing. Strongest runner-up is PGS002739 because it is also a direct AUD endpoint and shows a solid OR, but its much smaller variant set and slightly weaker OR make it less likely to rank #1 in the hidden benchmark.

Direct-match cluster is the incident atopic dermatitis endpoint (PGS002755, PGS004587): both are EUR-evaluated, same covariates, same very large validation sample (n=337,910), and both target incident AD rather than the therapy-specific paradoxical eczema endpoints (PGS003486/PGS003459/PGS004903) or the restricted moderate-to-severe Canadian cohort construct (PGS001773). Between the two incident-AD near-clones, PGS002755 is more likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants) that typically captures substantially more polygenic signal than a sparse genome-wide-significant-hits score (23 variants in PGS004587), and it also shows a stronger reported risk gradient (HR high vs low PRS 1.249 vs 1.153). Strongest runner-up is PGS004587 due to identical endpoint/validation context, but its very small SNP set and weaker HR make it less likely to be the top performer.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches for ankylosing spondylitis by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. The strongest evidence comes from the two near-clone UKB snpnet models (PGS001268, PGS001267) because they report PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC and PGS-only R²) with only basic covariates, enabling a cleaner comparison than the EAS-only Taiwanese models (which report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates) and the UKB portability scores (which report only partial-r). Between the two snpnet siblings, PGS001268 is more likely to rank #1 externally because it has consistently stronger PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC 0.7346 vs 0.7265; PGS-only R² 0.1023 vs 0.0988) and slightly higher full-model AUROC/R² on the same endpoint family and covariate set. Strongest runner-up: PGS001267, which is essentially the same design but with marginally weaker PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates map to autism spectrum disorder by trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000327 has clearly superior endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder” vs PGS002790’s “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”, which looks like a proxy/behavioral construct rather than a direct ASD case-control endpoint). PGS000327 also has stronger and more directly PRS-informative performance evidence in the visible record (R²=0.0245 plus an OR per SD of 1.33 with tight CI) and a larger evaluation sample (n=7,148 vs n=2,198), while keeping covariates basic (PCs/genotyping wave). The strongest runner-up is PGS002790 because SDPR with ~916k variants is a method/coverage advantage, but its weak partial R² (~0.0055) and, more importantly, the phenotype mismatch make it less likely to rank #1 in an external ASD benchmark than the disease-endpoint score PGS000327.

Direct-match cluster: PGS001263 is the only candidate with phenotyping_reported exactly matching the target trait (“Atrial flutter”) and trait_efo restricted to atrial flutter, avoiding the broader AF+flutter composite endpoint used by PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050. Within this shortlist, PGS001263 also has the strongest comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates 0.02517), with clean/basic covariates and performance that is plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling. Strongest runner-up: PGS001339, which has very similar snpnet framework context and metrics but is a broader time-to-event AF+flutter phenotype (less endpoint-fidelitous for pure atrial flutter) and slightly weaker PRS-only performance (AUROC 0.613; R2 0.02447). The portability-paper candidates (PGS001841/PGS002050) are also broader AF+flutter and lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, reporting only partial-r, making them less well-supported for ranking #1 in an external benchmark.

All shortlisted models are broadly direct matches for atrial fibrillation, but several are penalized as risk-wrapper/packaged endpoints (e.g., CHARGE-AF/ECG-AI 5-year risk) or pan-trait/portability frameworks. Within the clean, direct AF diagnosis cluster with comparable basic covariates, the MVP diverse-populations method-comparison set provides the strongest visible PRS-discrimination evidence via per-SD effect size. PGS005067 (PRS-CS) has the strongest reported per-SD OR (1.734, 95% CI 1.66–1.81) among the high-performing MVP siblings and a top-tier C-index (0.8276) in European evaluation with standard covariates (age, sex, PCs), making it the best-supported bet for #1 external benchmark performance. Strongest runner-up is PGS005072 (PRS-CSx), which has a very similar C-index (0.8264) but a slightly weaker OR (1.684); given same endpoint/covariates/validation context, the higher effect size is the decisive tie-break in favor of PGS005067.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches for angina pectoris, but the strongest same-endpoint cluster is the 2024 HGG Adv MVP-based PheCode 411.3 models (PGS005047–PGS005059), which share consistent phenotyping (Angina pectoris), clean/basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), and comparable evaluation context. Within this near-clone family, PGS005052 has the best combined visible performance signals: it is essentially tied for the top full-model C-index (0.766245) while also showing the strongest per-SD effect size (OR=1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57), which is a more PRS-informative discriminator than tiny C-index differences when covariates are identical. The strongest runner-up is PGS005048 (C-index 0.766876, OR=1.487), which has a marginally higher C-index but slightly weaker OR; given the same endpoint/covariates/validation size, the higher OR makes PGS005052 more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark. Older UKB sparse/framework scores (PGS001260/PGS001261/PGS001262) report PGS-only metrics but are from a pan-trait sparse-PRS archetype and are less reliably transferable than the coherent MVP disease-endpoint family; the Commun Biol metaPRS entries (PGS004527/PGS004457) lack comparable discrimination metrics and include integration/packaging risk.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and largely on phenotyping_reported (only PGS000753 is slightly less aligned as “Prevalent” AAA). The strongest PRS-comparable evidence in the pool is from PGS001784, which uniquely reports a PRS-only (covariates-regressed-out) Nagelkerke R²=0.014661 alongside a large EUR evaluation (n=350,767) and a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto, 911,440 variants). That PRS-only R² is also plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.02), suggesting the metric is informative rather than inflated. The strongest runner-up is PGS003973 (same AAA endpoint, PRS-CS, ~1.12M variants, disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis), but it only provides a full-model C-index (0.882) with basic covariates; without PRS-only/incremental metrics, that high discrimination is likely dominated by age/sex and is not reliably comparable for ranking PRS performance. PGS003429 and PGS003972 similarly rely on full-model AUROC only, and PGS002054 is a portability-framework score with only a weak partial-r (0.0144), making it less likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait PRS benchmark.

Direct-match cluster for aortic stenosis is PGS005252/PGS005254/PGS005256/PGS005255 (all have incident aortic stenosis in phenotyping_reported, whereas PGS000778/PGS000739/PGS004910/PGS004911 are hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and off-trait). Among the direct-match set, PGS005254 is most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark because it is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with strong per-SD time-to-event signal (HR=1.64, 95% CI 1.50–1.78) evaluated in a large EUR cohort (n=244,450) with only basic demographic/PC covariates, reducing risk that apparent performance is driven by heavy clinical adjustment. Strongest runner-up is PGS005252, which has a larger reported HR (1.92) and a high full-model C-index (0.87), but that record uses extensive clinical comorbidity covariates (T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure, etc.), making the discrimination less comparable to PRS-only benchmark settings and more prone to covariate-driven inflation; additionally its training sample is smaller than PGS005254 (47,691 vs 205,483).

All three candidates are plausible direct matches on trait_efo, but PGS004913 has the highest endpoint fidelity and study intent: phenotyping_reported is exactly “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis” and the publication is explicitly a cirrhosis PRS among heavy drinkers (disease-focused rather than a broad framework). Its reported effect size is also strong (OR top vs bottom deciles = 4.4), with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and EUR-only development/evaluation, reducing transport mismatch. Strongest runner-up is PGS000704 because it uses a methodologically strong genome-wide snpnet multi-PRS with very large development/validation and clean basic covariates; however, it comes from a broad biomarkers genetics paper (higher framework/indirect-optimization risk) and its visible genetic signal is only moderate (HR 1.18), while the reported full-model C-index (0.711) is not PRS-only and thus less comparable. PGS001777 is less supported due to an extremely sparse 3-variant score, unknown covariates, and a phenotype restriction (“Cirrhosis (males)”), making it less likely to top an external benchmark.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for asthma, but many are penalized by either (i) being framework-style scores (e.g., UKB sparse snpnet; global-biobank framework), (ii) being risk-factor integration/metaPRS packaging, or (iii) lacking PRS-comparable performance metrics. PGS001344 is the strongest direct-match record because it has high endpoint fidelity (doctor-diagnosed asthma), reports clear PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS-only R2=0.05973) with basic covariates, and its PRS-only R2 is substantial yet still plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.1515). The strongest runner-up is PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto, global-biobank framework), which has a strong covariates-regressed-out R2 (0.048844) and AUROC 0.659, but it is more framework-derived and has much smaller European validation (n=7,128) than PGS001344’s UKB-based doctor-diagnosed endpoint with stronger PRS-only R2 evidence; thus PGS001344 is more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

PGS002786 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly matches the target trait (bipolar disorder), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are explicitly subtype scores (bipolar I and bipolar II). All three are otherwise near-clones (same publication/date, SDPR method, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, similar variant counts, basic covariates), and their reported partial R² values are very close and not PRS-only metrics, so endpoint fidelity is the main differentiator. Strongest runner-up is PGS002787 (bipolar I) because it is closer to the umbrella diagnosis than bipolar II and has a slightly higher partial R² than PGS002786, but the subtype mismatch makes it less likely to rank #1 on a benchmark defined for broad bipolar disorder.

PGS001033 is the only candidate whose trait_efo directly matches the target concept (“blood coagulation disease”), and it also provides explicit PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and PGS R² 0.0578) rather than only a weak proxy metric. The strongest runner-up is PGS002034 because it targets a closely related coagulation-deficiency phenotype and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many variants, but it lacks any AUROC/R² and only reports a small partial correlation (~0.056), making it less well-supported for predicting top external-benchmark rank despite similar partial-r to PGS001826.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for celiac disease, but several are framework/portability scores (PGS001301; PGS002067/PGS001856; PGS002107/PGS001894) and two are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (PGS000041/PGS000042), which is a narrower endpoint than generic celiac disease. Among the direct, generic celiac disease endpoints, PGS000040 has the strongest visible discrimination evidence (full-model AUROC=0.90 in EUR evaluation) from a disease-focused study context, making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark despite missing explicit PGS-only metrics. The strongest runner-up is PGS001301 because it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.8287) and PGS-only R2 (0.1422), but it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework and uses a broader/administrative phenotype label (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), which is a higher-risk archetype for external transfer than the disease-focused celiac-specific model family represented by PGS000040.

Direct-match cluster: PGS002032 and PGS001824 are clean direct matches (trait_efo=bilirubin metabolism disease; phenotyping_reported=Disorders of bilirubin excretion). PGS000924 is a broader composite (porphyrin + bilirubin) and explicitly time-to-event, so it’s a weaker endpoint match despite having reported AUROC/R².

Between the two direct-match siblings (same publication family, same training cohort/size, same covariates, same validation ancestry/size, and identical partial-r=0.0716), the only meaningful differentiator is method/structure: PGS002032 uses LDpred2 with genome-wide shrinkage and far more variants (19,768) versus PGS001824’s penalized regression with 22 variants. With identical observed performance in the visible record, the higher-capacity genome-wide shrinkage model is more likely to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark.

Strongest runner-up: PGS001824, because it is equally endpoint-faithful and has the same observed partial-r; it loses on structural grounds (very sparse 22-variant model) when the empirical metrics are tied.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly direct matches for basal cell carcinoma except PGS005207, which is explicitly a restricted survivorship/treatment-exposed endpoint (“Risk of basal cell carcinoma in childhood cancer survivors”) and thus less endpoint-faithful for generic BCC risk. Within the main direct-match cluster (mostly Cancer PRSweb models with identical basic covariates), PGS000454 is the strongest on the most comparable visible performance evidence: it ties for the top full-model AUROC (0.632) while having the highest (or essentially highest) Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0489) among the MGI-evaluated siblings, plus strong effect sizes (OR per SD 1.661; top 1% vs rest OR 3.79). The strongest runner-up is PGS000452, which is nearly a clone (same endpoint, cohort context, covariates, and AUROC 0.632) but is marginally weaker on the key tie-breakers (pseudo-R² 0.0487 vs 0.0489; top 1% OR 3.61 vs 3.79), making PGS000454 slightly more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

Direct-match cluster is the cholelithiasis ICD10 K80 models (PGS004546, PGS004476) plus closely related cholelithiasis/cholecystitis models (PGS002072, PGS001861) and the time-to-event cholelithiasis model (PGS001174); PGS005150 is EAS-only evaluation and less likely to win a generic external benchmark unless that benchmark is EAS-specific. Among the strongest direct K80 matches, PGS004546 and PGS004476 share the same study family, endpoint (K80), EUR-only dev/eval, and identical genome-wide variant count, so the main differentiator is effect-size evidence: PGS004546 reports a materially higher per-SD OR (1.2986 vs 1.2194), making it more likely to rank #1 in a hidden same-trait benchmark. Strongest runner-up is PGS004476 because it is the closest near-clone on endpoint/method/context; it loses on the only visible within-family performance signal (lower OR).

PGS003428 is the strongest direct-match cervical carcinoma PRS in the shortlist because it is a disease-focused, endpoint-faithful model (incident cervical cancer) built with a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred) and very large variant coverage (~2.9M), with supportive PRS-linked effect size evidence (HR per SD 1.33) in a large European evaluation (n=128,113). This combination (high-fidelity endpoint + genome-wide method + nontrivial per-SD HR) is more predictive of topping an external same-trait benchmark than relying on covariate-inflated full-model discrimination from sparse GWAS-hit scores.

Strongest runner-up: PGS000073 (and its near-clone PGS000784). They share the same incident cervical cancer endpoint and show higher reported full-model AUROC/C-index (~0.745), but they are 10-SNP genome-wide-significant hit scores with relatively modest HR (~1.22) and heavier epidemiologic covariate packaging; without PRS-only metrics, their apparent AUROC advantage is likely driven largely by covariates rather than stronger standalone PRS signal, making them less likely than PGS003428 to rank #1 in a PRS-performance benchmark.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for breast carcinoma, but several are clearly off-target subtypes (ER+/ER−/triple-negative) or special-population endpoints (e.g., BRCA1 carriers <40, breast cancer-specific survival), which are weaker direct matches for generic breast carcinoma risk. Within the strongest direct-match cluster (generic “Breast cancer” / “Breast cancer (female)” diagnosis endpoints), the 2023 five-biobank method-evaluation family provides the most comparable, PRS-forward evidence with covariates explicitly set to 0 and consistent effect-size reporting. Among those near-clones, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the best visible performance package: highest full-model AUROC (~0.6625) and highest reported R² (~0.0764) with the strongest per-SD effect size (OR ~1.826) in the same evaluation context (EUR validation, n~48,968). The strongest runner-up is PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV), which is extremely close (AUROC ~0.6598; R² ~0.0739; OR ~1.809), but it is slightly weaker on both discrimination and effect size within the same study/context, making PGS004153 the most likely #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

PGS004621 is the strongest direct match to the target (trait_efo = cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported = Cirrhosis) and is built with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.09M variants), which is a strong structural predictor of external performance when PRS-only metrics are not available. It also shows a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.42) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and it comes from a disease-focused multi-cohort cirrhosis genetics study, reducing the risk that performance is an artifact of a pan-trait framework or heavy clinical packaging.

Strongest runner-up: PGS000726, which is also a direct cirrhosis match and is developed in a multi-cohort setting with a reasonable per-SD OR (1.32) and a top-vs-bottom quintile OR (2.26). However, it is a sparse GWAS-hits score (12 variants) with no comparable discrimination metric reported, making it less likely than the genome-wide PRS-CS model (PGS004621) to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark for generic cirrhosis of liver.

Direct-match cluster includes PGS001334/PGS001332/PGS001333 (snpnet UKB 813-traits framework), PGS001850/PGS002062 (UKB portability framework), PGS001788/PGS001783 (Global Biobank PRS-CS-auto COPD), and PGS004466/PGS004536 (J44 COPD from risk-factor-integration paper). Among these, the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence is in the Global Biobank PRS-CS-auto pair: PGS001783 reports the highest covariates-regressed-out/Nagelkerke R2 (0.038092) and the highest reported AUROC (0.74) within that same endpoint/method family, aligning well with the COPD heritability ceiling (h2_liability~0.0388) without exceeding it—suggesting a strong, plausible PRS signal rather than covariate-driven discrimination. The strongest runner-up is PGS001788 (same study/method/endpoint) but it has materially lower PRS R2 (0.0163) and lower AUROC (0.715), making it less likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark. The UKB framework/portability scores have weaker PRS-only metrics (or only partial-r) and the Commun Biol integration models lack comparable PRS-only metrics and carry packaging risk, so they are less likely to win despite recency or OR reporting.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale: Both candidates are direct matches (identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), from the same UKB portability study, with the same training cohort, covariates, validation ancestry context, and essentially identical partial-r (0.0563 vs 0.0562), so performance evidence is a tie. The best differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 (genome-wide shrinkage) with far more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is more likely to capture polygenic signal and edge out in an external benchmark when endpoints and evaluation are otherwise the same. Strongest runner-up: PGS001826, which is similarly supported but is a much sparser penalized-regression score with no metric advantage to justify preferring it over the LDpred2 sibling.

Both candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/efo/phenotyping all corneal dystrophy) from the same UKB portability paper with identical training cohort, covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation size, so the decision hinges on within-family performance and structural signals. PGS002042 is more likely to rank #1 because it shows stronger PRS-comparable performance in the selected European validation record (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384 for PGS001835) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is generally a positive structural indicator when endpoints and evaluation context are otherwise identical. Strongest runner-up: PGS001835, but its lower partial-r and extremely sparse variant set make it less likely to outperform the LDpred2 sibling in an external same-trait benchmark.

All three candidates are direct Crohn’s disease matches by trait_efo/phenotyping, but PGS004254’s apparent advantage (full-model AUROC=0.72) is not PRS-comparable because it lacks PGS-only AUROC/R² and incremental metrics; with only basic covariates shown, it could still be partly covariate-driven and is harder to benchmark fairly against PRS-only-reported models. Between the two near-clone snpnet framework scores (same publication family, same training cohort, same validation N and covariates), PGS001331 is the stronger sibling: higher PGS-only AUROC (0.579 vs 0.576), higher PGS-only R² (0.00677 vs 0.00621), and higher incremental AUROC (0.0271 vs 0.0241), making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark. Strongest runner-up: PGS001330 (same context but consistently weaker metrics).

PGS002237 is the best-supported direct-match CKD PRS because it is a disease-focused score explicitly targeting clinically defined CKD stage 3+ (eGFR <45), trained at much larger scale (n=279,819) and showing strong discriminative evidence for the PRS contribution via a high per-SD effect size (OR=1.47) alongside strong reported discrimination (AUROC=0.78) in European validation. Many other candidates either (a) lack comparable PRS-forward performance evidence (e.g., PGS005113, PGS002757, PGS000728), (b) are endpoint-mismatched/proxy (eGFR rather than CKD diagnosis for PGS000728), or (c) are benchmarking-paper siblings with only modest full-model AUROCs ~0.55–0.59 and no PGS-only metrics (PGS004158/PGS004074/PGS004030 etc.), making them less likely to top an external same-trait benchmark. Strongest runner-up is PGS004158 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV), which is endpoint-aligned and has the best full-model AUROC/R² within the five-biobank benchmarking cluster (AUROC~0.592; R²~0.020), but that cluster’s absolute performance is much lower and is harder to interpret as PRS-driven (no PGS-only metrics), whereas PGS002237’s disease-focused design and materially stronger effect/discrimination package is more predictive of #1 benchmark ranking.

Direct-match cluster for target_trait=arthritis is limited to the generic arthritis EFO candidates: PGS001135 (Arthritis (nos), snpnet) and the two Commun Biol integration-study models PGS004547/PGS004477 (M13 Other arthritis; RFDiseasemetaPRS / LDpred2). I exclude the many gout/RA/osteoarthritis/ankylosing/psoriatic/JIA scores as off-trait (they are specific arthritis subtypes rather than generic arthritis). Between the direct-match candidates, PGS001135 is the only one with PRS-comparable metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R2=0.00291), whereas PGS004547/PGS004477 provide only a single OR from a risk-factor-integration framework with no standalone PRS discrimination metrics, increasing packaging/comparability risk for a hidden external PRS benchmark. Strongest runner-up is PGS004547 (same EFO=arthritis and slightly higher reported OR than PGS004477), but it is less likely to rank #1 externally because its evidence is effect-size-only within an integrated disease+risk-factor metaPRS context and lacks PRS-only performance reporting.

Direct-match cluster is the major-depressive-disorder / depressive-disorder PRSs with disease-status endpoints (excluding clearly off-trait/treatment/brain-imaging proxies like PGS000907, PGS000767, PGS003442, and excluding bipolar PGS002786). Within the strongest same-endpoint family (the multiple UKB-developed PRSice-2 ‘MDD (Lifetime)’ scores from the same 2023 phenotype-integration study), PGS003578 has the highest reported R² (0.0257) under essentially identical endpoint/covariate context (PCs 1–10, EUR validation), making it the best-supported bet to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark. Strongest runner-up is PGS003580 (R²=0.0254) from the same study family and near-identical setup; it narrowly loses on the only meaningful differentiator available here (slightly lower R²).

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches for dilated cardiomyopathy; the main plausible cluster is the 2024-12-16 Nat Genet family with explicit PRS-only AUC/OR and clean, minimal covariates. Within that cluster, PGS004951 is most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark because it combines strong PRS-only discrimination (univariate/PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI 0.65–0.69), the strongest effect size signal in the EUR-evaluated set (OR per SD=1.93; β=0.66), and a direct clinical DCM phenotype with only sex+PC covariates (low leakage risk). Strongest runner-up is PGS004949, which has slightly higher PRS-only AUC (0.68) and similar OR (1.91) but is evaluated in MAE-only and uses a non-ischemic DCM phenotype; that evaluation/endpoint shift makes it less reliable for a generic dilated cardiomyopathy benchmark than the EUR-evaluated clinical DCM score in PGS004951.

All five candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease/K57, but PGS004614 is the only clearly disease-focused score (Cell Genomics diverticular disease study) using a genome-wide shrinkage method (SBayesR; ~1.08M variants), which is structurally more likely to transfer and rank #1 than the UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet scores. Its reported AUROC=0.76 is full-model and includes family history (so it is discounted as PRS evidence), yet the combination of disease-specific study archetype + genome-wide model still best predicts top external benchmark performance. Strongest runner-up: PGS000997, because it provides explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.591, PGS R2 0.0178) and clean/basic covariates; however it comes from the '813 traits' sparse UKB framework (known to generalize worse) and its PRS-only signal is only modest, making it less likely than PGS004614 to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark.

Direct-match cluster for target trait dementia is led by candidates with trait_efo=dementia and phenotyping_reported as dementia endpoints (PGS000946, PGS000929, PGS001827, PGS002035, PGS004282/PGS004281/PGS004283/PGS004284, PGS004318, PGS005170). Excluding clearly off-trait biomarker/cognition proxies and Alzheimer-only endpoints, PGS000946 is best-supported because it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64149; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02543; incremental AUROC=0.02339) on a large EUR validation (n=67,425) with standard covariates, giving the strongest standalone-PRS evidence among dementia-labeled candidates. Strongest runner-up is PGS000929 (all-cause dementia algorithmically-defined), which is similarly aligned and validated but has slightly weaker PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC=0.62703; PGS R2=0.02346; incremental AUROC=0.02294). GenoBoost all-cause dementia models (e.g., PGS004281/PGS004284/PGS004282/PGS004283) show higher full-model AUROC (~0.818) but lack PGS-only/incremental metrics, making their apparent advantage likely covariate-driven and less comparable for predicting #1 external PRS benchmark performance.

All three candidates are direct matches for Dupuytren contracture by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS002092 and PGS001880 are near-clones from the same UKB portability study with identical endpoint, covariates, training cohort, and validation context; the key differentiators are method/structure and the reported PRS-comparable metric. PGS002092 (LDpred2, genome-wide shrinkage; 484,484 variants) has a slightly higher partial correlation (0.0797 vs 0.0783) than its strongest runner-up PGS001880 (penalized regression; 2,443 variants), and its much denser genome-wide construction is the more reliable structural bet for ranking #1 in an external same-trait benchmark when endpoints and evaluation are otherwise identical. PGS001254 reports explicit AUROC/R², but it comes from the sparse pan-trait UKB framework (snpnet; 11 variants), which is a known weaker archetype for external transfer despite cleaner metric reporting; its apparent advantage is therefore less predictive than the same-endpoint, same-context LDpred2 vs penalized-regression comparison between PGS002092 and PGS001880.

Direct-match cluster is PGS002304, PGS000643, and PGS000644 (all map to follicular lymphoma; PGS000643/PGS000644 use the near-synonymous ‘nodular lymphoma’ phenotype consistent with follicular [nodular] lymphoma). PGS003455 is excluded because phenotyping_reported is ‘Chronic lymphocytic leukemia’, an explicit endpoint mismatch despite the follicular-lymphoma label fields. Between the two same-study near-clones (PGS000643 PRS-CS vs PGS000644 lassosum; same cohorts, covariates, ancestry, and validation size), PGS000644 has slightly better full-model AUROC (0.538 vs 0.532), higher pseudo-R² (0.00349 vs 0.00282), and a slightly stronger per-SD OR (1.149 vs 1.133), making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark. Strongest runner-up is PGS000643, but it is consistently weaker on the comparable within-family metrics; PGS002304’s higher full-model AUROC (0.61) is not PRS-comparable and is supported by a very small validation n=197 with unknown covariates, so it is less reliable for predicting top external PRS performance.

Direct-match cluster includes the glaucoma/POAG scores; exclude clearly weaker non-PRS constructions (e.g., tiny GWAS-hit sets like PGS000350/PGS002741, and the 23-SNP catalog-selected score PGS000764). Among the remaining genome-wide PRS candidates, PGS004766 (PRSmixPlus) is the strongest structural bet for #1 hidden-benchmark performance: it is a modern integrative/mixture PRS method with genome-wide coverage (~838k variants), clean basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), and a reported incremental R2 of 0.031 in EUR evaluation—competitive with the best PRS-only R2 signals shown here (e.g., PGS001792 Nagelkerke R2=0.03209) while avoiding the ‘pan-trait sparse UKB’ penalty affecting the snpnet glaucoma models (PGS001322/PGS001323). Strongest runner-up is PGS001792 (PRS-CS-auto, POAG) because it has very large evaluation N and similar PRS-only R2, but it comes from a global-biobank framework context and targets POAG specifically; PGS004766 is a direct glaucoma endpoint in the same ancestry with an integrative method that is more likely to edge out in an external same-trait benchmark.

Within the direct-match CAD cluster (trait_efo=coronary artery disease; phenotyping_reported=coronary artery disease), PGS003725 is best-supported for likely #1 external benchmark performance because it comes from a disease-focused, multi-ancestry PRS construction context (LDpred2; genome-wide scale variant count ~1.3M; broad multi-cohort training_development_cohorts) and shows the strongest visible per-SD effect size evidence among the closest like-for-like candidates (HR=1.75 and OR=2.14). This combination (endpoint fidelity + genome-wide shrinkage method + strong effect size) is the most predictive package here when PRS-only AUC/R2 are largely missing across the shortlist.

Strongest runner-up: PGS003726 (same Nat Med multi-ancestry CAD family; LDpred2; similar endpoint/covariates/validation context) with HR=1.73. PGS003725 is preferred because it has slightly stronger effect-size evidence (HR 1.75 vs 1.73, plus an explicit OR 2.14) in an otherwise near-clone context, making it more likely to rank #1 in a hidden same-trait benchmark.

Direct-match cluster is the heart-failure / congestive-heart-failure candidates (excluding the cor pulmonale / pulmonary heart disease scores). Within the strongest coherent same-endpoint family (MVP PheCode 428.1 CHF, NOS; age/sex/20 PCs; same eval n=31,804 EUR), PGS005077 stands out with the best reported discrimination (full-model C-index 0.7536) and the strongest per-SD effect size signal (OR 1.452, 95% CI 1.38–1.53), which is a strong tie-break among near-clones sharing essentially identical endpoint and covariates. Strongest runner-up is PGS005083 (same endpoint/context) with nearly identical C-index (0.7537) and OR (1.455), but PGS005077 is slightly more internally consistent as the top-performing ldpred sibling and edges on the combined metric+effect-size package versus the prscs sibling where small differences are likely noise; overall this makes PGS005077 the most likely #1 in an external same-trait benchmark among the shortlist.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = Hashimoto's thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same study family with the same evaluation ancestry mix and validation N, so the decision hinges on within-family performance/effect-size signals rather than endpoint differences. PGS005271 (PRS-CS, ~1.085M variants) has the strongest discriminative evidence among the PRS-CS siblings: higher full-model AUROC (0.6297 vs 0.6054 for PGS005272) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.55 vs 1.42), which is a more PRS-informative signal than small AUROC shifts when PGS-only metrics are absent. The strongest runner-up is PGS005270 because it has the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.6387), but it is a sparse P+T score with only 55 variants and a near-null reported OR (1.037), making that AUROC likely less reflective of true PRS signal and less likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark than the stronger-effect, genome-wide PRS-CS model.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for hip osteoarthritis/coxarthrosis, but several are weaker proxies or have packaging risk: PGS002728 and PGS002750 use hip replacement/total hip replacement (treatment proxy), and PGS004548 is an integrated metaPRS (risk-factor + disease) rather than a clean disease PRS. Among the direct disease-endpoint PRSs, PGS002763 has the strongest PRS-discrimination evidence via a comparatively high per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46) on an explicitly matched phenotype (“Hip osteoarthritis”), built with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) and evaluated in EUR with standard demographic/PC/technical covariates—an evidence package that tends to transfer well. Strongest runner-up is PGS004882 (incident hip osteoarthritis; HR=1.4 with huge evaluation N), but its reported metric is a full-model C-index (0.6) with no PRS-only metric, and its development context (DEV n=404; 1000G) plus incidence-only framing makes its apparent strength less directly comparable; overall PGS002763 is more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

Direct-match cluster is the gout/gout-efo candidates with phenotyping_reported as gout (excluding clear endpoint shifts like age-at-onset-only PGS003329 and heavy non-PRS packaging/interaction studies like PGS002307/PGS004222). Within the direct gout PRS set, PGS001789 is most likely to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark because it provides the strongest PRS-comparable evidence (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.031208) alongside a strong full-model AUROC (0.807) and, critically, it is developed/validated in a broad multi-biobank/global context with very large evaluation support (n=359,345), which is a strong transferability signal versus single-cohort method papers. Strongest runner-up is PGS001248 (snpnet), which has slightly higher PRS-only R2 (0.04014) and strong full-model AUROC (0.81572) but comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework that empirically generalizes less well; its apparent edge is more likely to be UKB-optimized rather than robustly portable. GenoBoost siblings (e.g., PGS004269/PGS004266) show high full-model AUROC (~0.799) but lack PRS-only metrics and are therefore less reliably supported for cross-model ranking.

Direct-match cluster for Hodgkins lymphoma is the Cancer PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease set: PGS000637 (PRS-CS), PGS000638 (GWAS Hits), PGS000639 (P+T), PGS000640 (lassosum). All share the same endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Hodgkin’s disease), EUR-only context, and only basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), so their reported full-model metrics are at least comparably adjusted. Within this near-clone family, PGS000639 has the strongest visible discrimination/effect package (full-model AUROC 0.62 and the highest Nagelkerke R² 0.0276, plus OR per SD 1.476), making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark among the direct Hodgkin lymphoma candidates. Strongest runner-up is PGS000638 (GWAS Hits), which is close but has slightly lower AUROC (0.601) and lower R² (0.0193), so it is less supported as the top performer given otherwise identical study/endpoint/covariate context.

Both candidates are direct matches (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), from the same UKB portability study, with identical training size, covariates, and validation context—so the key differentiators are the PRS-comparable metric and structural method/variant coverage. PGS002031 has a slightly higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.1355 vs 0.1307 for PGS001823) in the selected European validation record and uses LDpred2 with substantially more variants (6713 vs 654), which is a favorable structural signal when endpoints and evaluation are otherwise the same. Strongest runner-up: PGS001823; it is very similar but has marginally weaker partial-r and a much sparser penalized-regression score, making it less likely to rank #1 in the hidden same-trait benchmark.

All four candidates are direct-match on trait_efo (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), but PGS004911 has the strongest overall evidence package for likely top external-benchmark performance: it is a genome-wide PRS-CS score (374,114 variants) with large EUR evaluation (n=343,182) and the best reported discrimination/effect evidence among the comparable PRS-CS siblings (full-model AUROC 0.80; R² 0.048; HR 2.34; high-vs-median-tertile OR 5.9). The strongest runner-up is PGS004910 (same paper, same covariates, near-identical variant count), but it is consistently weaker on the visible performance signals (AUROC 0.73; R² 0.031; HR 1.97; tertile OR 5.5), making PGS004911 the more likely #1 in a same-trait benchmark. PGS000739’s AUROC is full-model and heavily covariate-augmented (multiple clinical risk factors plus rare-variant carrier status), reducing comparability to PRS performance; PGS000778 is a sparse 20-variant score with small validation and a restricted phenotype (events among sarcomeric-variant carriers), making it less likely to generalize as the top-performing general-population HCM PRS.

Direct-match cluster for hyperthyroidism includes the thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism scores (PGS001042, PGS001043, PGS002023, PGS001815) and the Graves’ disease scores (PGS005264, PGS005265, PGS005266), with Graves’ disease being a clinically dominant hyperthyroidism subtype and thus an acceptable direct match. Within the Graves’ disease family (same publication/context, same evaluation sample size and ancestry context), PGS005265 is the strongest sibling: it has the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.6652 vs 0.6637 for PGS005266 and 0.6587 for PGS005264) and, more importantly, the strongest per-SD effect size signal (OR 1.625 vs 1.543; PGS005264’s OR≈1.01 is effectively null), which is a better proxy for PRS discriminative strength when PRS-only AUC/R² are not provided. The strongest runner-up is PGS001043 (hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis snpnet), which reports explicit PGS-only AUROC/R², but it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework and its PRS-only R² (~0.022) is modest; given the domain guidance that disease-focused multi-cohort scores with strong effect sizes typically transfer better than sparse framework scores, PGS005265 is more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark despite lacking PRS-only metrics.

Winner PGS002336 because it is a clean, direct-match hypothyroidism endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Hypothyroidism) with a genome-wide method (BOLT-LMM; 1,109,311 variants) and the strongest PRS-comparable performance signal available in the main direct-match cluster: incremental R2=0.0247 in a reasonably sized EUR validation (n=43,505) with only basic demographic/PC/array covariates. This combination (endpoint fidelity + strong genome-wide construction + best incremental-R2 among comparable UKB-based direct hypothyroidism models) is most predictive of topping an external benchmark.

Strongest runner-up: PGS002653 (PolyFun-pred; incremental R2=0.0262) is close on incremental R2, but its metric is explicitly ‘when combined with BOLT-LMM’, making it a bundled/stacked context rather than a standalone score signal; that packaging risk makes it less likely to rank #1 in a generic external same-trait benchmark than the standalone BOLT-LMM score. PGS005218 reports a much higher AUROC (0.859) but it is a biomarker-heavy full model (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), so that AUROC is not comparable as PRS performance evidence and is discounted for benchmark ranking.

PGS000114 is the only candidate that directly matches the target umbrella endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to juvenile idiopathic arthritis rather than a specific subtype), making it the most endpoint-faithful choice for a generic JIA benchmark. All four are same publication/method/ancestry/covariate context (SparSNP; EUR dev/eval; sex+PCs), so the key differentiator is phenotype alignment; within that constraint PGS000114 also shows solid supporting discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.738) and a strong per-SD effect size (OR 2.085). Strongest runner-up is PGS000325 (oligoarticular JIA) because it has a higher AUROC (0.80) and large validation N, but it is a subtype-specific endpoint and thus less likely to rank #1 on a hidden benchmark defined on overall JIA cases.

Direct-match cluster for hypertension includes multiple ExPRSweb framework scores (e.g., PGS002994/PGS002998/PGS002996/PGS002995), UKB sparse/portability scores (PGS001320/PGS000957/PGS000958/PGS002047/PGS001838), and several disease-focused hypertension PRS from dedicated studies (notably PGS004236/PGS004234 from a multi-ethnic hypertension paper, plus PGS004787/PGS004785 etc.). Among these, PGS004236 is the best-supported for likely top external benchmark performance because it is a disease-focused, multi-ethnic hypertension PRS with strong reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.764) and a large effect size (OR 2.10), with broad validation (n=39,035) and covariates that are standard demographic/ancestry/BMI adjustments rather than heavy clinical risk packaging. The strongest runner-up is PGS002998 (ExPRSweb PRS-CS; AUROC 0.63; OR 1.67), which has decent effect size but comes from a pan-trait/framework repository context that empirically under-transfers versus disease-focused models; additionally its reported AUROC is much lower than PGS004236’s and it lacks multi-ethnic external-validation framing. Therefore PGS004236 is more likely to rank #1 in a hidden same-trait external benchmark.

All shortlisted models are direct matches for kidney cancer/renal carcinoma/renal cell carcinoma, so the decision hinges on which record best predicts top external benchmark performance. PGS004908 is the strongest overall package: it is disease-focused (kidney cancer GWAS), uses a substantially larger GWAS-hits set (107 SNPs vs ~10–19 for most other GWAS-significant scores here), shows the strongest per-SD effect size (OR=1.5, 95% CI 1.43–1.58) and the best reported discrimination among candidates that provide AUROC (full-model AUROC=0.74, EUR eval). The covariate set is standard (age/sex/PCs plus common risk factors), reducing concern that performance is purely a clinical-risk wrapper.

Strongest runner-up: PGS000076 (and its near-clone PGS000787). It has excellent endpoint fidelity (incident kidney cancer) and huge evaluation size, but its per-SD effect (HR~1.16) and reported full-model AUROC (~0.722) are weaker than PGS004908, and it is an older, smaller-variant GWAS-significant score (19 variants). Given the materially stronger effect size and larger susceptibility-variant set in PGS004908 within the same direct-trait cluster, PGS004908 is more likely to rank #1 in a hidden same-trait benchmark.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for knee osteoarthritis/gonarthrosis, except PGS002749 which is a treatment/proxy endpoint (total knee replacement) and thus less direct for generic knee OA risk. Among the strongest direct-match cluster (PGS002767, PGS004479, PGS004883, PGS002729, PGS004549, plus the framework-style PGS001192), PGS004549 is most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark because it combines a genome-wide model (1,059,939 variants) with the strongest available per-SD effect size signal in the pool (OR=1.3667) on a directly aligned gonarthrosis endpoint in a large EUR evaluation (n=56,192). The strongest runner-up is PGS002767 (PRS-CS; OR=1.35; n=39,444), which is similarly endpoint-faithful and methodologically strong, but it has slightly weaker effect-size evidence and no other compensating PRS-only metric advantage. PGS004479 is a near-clone sibling (same endpoint family, similar variant count) but has a lower OR (1.323), making it less likely than PGS004549 to top the hidden benchmark.

PGS004606 is the strongest direct-match for macular degeneration because it targets the exact clinical endpoint (age-related macular degeneration), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS study archetype (not a pan-trait/portability framework), and shows strong PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.76 with tight CI) alongside a large external-style evaluation sample (n=163,011) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). The strongest runner-up is PGS004952, which reports a much higher AUROC (0.842) but only as a full-model metric in a very small validation set (n=1,232) and with a weaker OR (1.41), making it less reliable for predicting #1 performance in a hidden external benchmark. Framework-derived UKB scores (PGS001013, PGS002041, PGS001834) are penalized for study archetype and/or weak PRS-comparable metrics (e.g., partial-r ~0.016–0.018; PGS-only R2 ~0.006), and PGS004607 underperforms PGS004606 on both AUROC (0.65 vs 0.71) and OR (1.48 vs 1.76) in the same publication context.

Direct-match cluster is the systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) diagnosis endpoints (PGS000754, PGS004917, PGS003960, PGS000196), while several others are clearly subtype/restricted endpoints (renal disease, renal age-of-onset, early-onset <20, lupus nephritis class V, ACR criteria count) or portability-framework lupus (PGS002082, PGS001870). Within the direct SLE-diagnosis set, PGS000754 is most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage-style approach (lassosum) with very large variant count (~294k), which is a strong structural predictor of transferable PRS performance when PGS-only metrics are absent across the pool. Its reported full-model AUROC (0.65) is competitive and not an extreme outlier likely driven by heavy clinical covariates (covariates are unknown rather than explicitly phenotype-derived). The strongest runner-up is PGS004917 (AUROC 0.696, OR 2.01), but it is a sparse clumped GWAS-hits score (97 variants) with unclear training context (samples_training N/A, empty cohort list) and a study framed around gene–smoking interactions, increasing risk that the reported discrimination is context-specific and less robust than a genome-wide PRS in a generic external benchmark.

All five candidates map to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease by trait_efo, but only a subset are clean direct disease endpoints in phenotyping_reported. PGS002289 is excluded as non-direct (cognition-by-age interaction phenotype rather than LOAD case/control). PGS004918 is a pathway-restricted 8-SNP score with very small training/validation (n=439 train; n=136 eval) and only a full-model AUROC (0.731) with unknown covariates, making its apparent performance hard to interpret and unlikely to transfer. Between the remaining direct-match disease scores (PGS000054, PGS000053, PGS000334), PGS000054 has the strongest PRS-discrimination evidence via effect size (OR=1.73 per SD, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) with basic covariates (age, sex) and a reasonably sized external evaluation (n=3,324) in a non-EUR (AMR/Hispanic/Latin American) setting, which is supportive of robustness rather than overfitting to EUR-only evaluation. Strongest runner-up is PGS000334 because it is endpoint-aligned and EUR-evaluated with an R² reported (0.191), but that R² is a full-model/unspecified R² from a C+T score and is suspiciously high relative to the provided local h2_obs ceiling (0.0084), reducing trust in comparability; it also lacks an OR/HR signal. PGS000053 is the closest sibling to the winner but has a materially weaker OR (1.29), making PGS000054 more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches for multiple sclerosis by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported. The strongest evidence for likely top external benchmark performance comes from PGS002726: it is disease-focused (Brain paper on MS susceptibility/phenotype in Europeans), shows the best reported discrimination among the MS-specific candidates (full-model AUROC 0.80 with a very large top-decile risk enrichment OR=15.0), and is not a pan-trait/portability framework score. The strongest runner-up is PGS000809, which is also disease-focused and reports decent full-model AUROC (0.765) and R² (0.069), but its discrimination and effect-size evidence are weaker than PGS002726’s (lower AUROC and no comparable high OR enrichment). Framework-derived UKB portability/sparse models (PGS002038/PGS001831 partial-r ~0.04; PGS001270/PGS001271 modest PGS-only AUROC/R²) are penalized for archetype and typically underperform disease-focused MS scores in external benchmarks despite cleaner PRS-only metrics.

PGS004512 is the strongest direct-match lung cancer PRS in the shortlist because it targets the exact ICD-coded lung cancer endpoint (C34 malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung), is developed/evaluated in EUR with a large UKB-based development sample (n=174,489) and sizable evaluation (n=56,192), uses a multi-score aggregation approach (RFDiseasemetaPRS; structurally favored vs single-score constructions), and shows the strongest per-SD effect size among the clean same-endpoint siblings (OR=1.316). The strongest runner-up is PGS004442 from the same publication/endpoint/ancestry/variant-count context (LDpred2, OR=1.168); despite LDpred2 being a strong single-score method, the winner’s materially larger per-SD OR and ensemble/meta-PRS structure make it more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark. Very high full-model AUROCs in other candidates (e.g., PGS004860, PGS000078/PGS000789) are discounted because they are full-model and likely heavily covariate-driven, with no PRS-only metrics to confirm standalone PRS superiority.

Direct-match cluster is PGS000652/PGS000653/PGS000654/PGS002281/PGS002306 (all have trait_reported and phenotyping_reported as multiple myeloma with matching EFO). PGS003450 is excluded as off-trait because phenotyping_reported is chronic lymphocytic leukemia despite the myeloma label.

Among the direct matches, PGS002281 is best-supported for likely #1 external benchmark performance because it comes from a myeloma-focused PRS study and shows the strongest large-sample discrimination signal in a reasonably sized European validation (full-model AUROC 0.644 with tight CI; OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles), with only basic demographic/geography covariates (age, sex, region) and no obvious clinical-risk packaging. The Cancer PRSweb siblings (PGS000652/PGS000653/PGS000654) have materially weaker full-model AUROC (~0.55–0.58) and modest per-SD OR (~1.24–1.33), suggesting lower standalone PRS signal.

Strongest runner-up: PGS002306, which reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but is supported by a very small validation sample (n=290) and has unknown covariates, making that AUROC less reliable/transferable as evidence of PRS strength than PGS002281’s more stable, disease-focused validation package.

Both candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = nicotine dependence; phenotyping_reported = Tobacco use disorder) from the same UKB portability paper with the same training cohort, covariates, and European-selected validation context, so the key differentiators are the PRS-comparable metric and structural method properties. PGS002037 (LDpred2) shows a higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741 vs 0.0557 for PGS001830) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is generally a positive signal for capturing polygenic signal and transferring better when endpoints/covariates are otherwise identical. Strongest runner-up is PGS001830, but its sparser penalized regression score has weaker reported partial-r in the same study context, making it less likely to rank #1 in the hidden benchmark.

Direct-match cluster: melanoma / cutaneous melanoma / melanomas of skin (dx/hx) candidates; exclude clearly off-trait keratinocyte/BCC/SCC/non-melanoma skin cancer and broad skin cancer/carcinoma bundles. Within the direct melanoma set, PGS002253 has strong endpoint fidelity (incident invasive melanoma), very large independent evaluation support (n=395,647), and solid discrimination evidence (full-model AUROC 0.662 with minimal covariates: age, sex) plus an explicit PRS contribution signal (R²=0.051) that is plausibly within the trait’s heritability ceiling and more PRS-informative than full-model AUROC alone. Strongest runner-up is PGS003382 (skin cutaneous melanoma) with higher reported AUROC (0.682) and large n, but it lacks PRS-only/comparable metrics (only full-model AUROC and a small R²=0.0261) and comes from a broader pan-cancer germline-variant context, making its apparent edge less reliably attributable to the PRS itself than PGS002253’s more directly melanoma-focused external evaluation record.

Direct-match cluster is the set of myocardial-infarction–endpoint scores (trait_efo=myocardial infarction / acute myocardial infarction; phenotyping_reported=Myocardial infarction or I21). Within that cluster, the MVP-based HGG Adv method-comparison siblings (PGS005034/35/36/37/38/39 and PRS-CS/PRS-CSx variants) are the most coherent disease-endpoint family with comparable covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs) and like-for-like evaluation context, so their within-family performance/effect-size differences are the strongest tie-break. PGS005039 has the highest reported full-model C-index (0.78484) among the near-clone MI PheCode 411.2 ldpred scores and also the strongest per-SD effect size (OR=1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67), edging out the closest runner-up PGS005045 (C-index 0.78385; OR 1.554). UKB snpnet MI scores (e.g., PGS001317) report PRS-only AUROC/R2 but come from a pan-trait sparse framework and are less likely to transfer as well as this disease-focused multi-ancestry-trained MI family; CVD/CAD composite endpoints (e.g., PGS000117/PGS005253) are not as phenotype-faithful to myocardial infarction specifically.

Both candidates are direct matches to the target (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp) with identical endpoint fields, same publication family, same EUR-only UKB development/evaluation context, same variant count, and similarly missing PRS-comparable AUC/R2—so the main differentiator is the available PRS signal proxy (per-SD effect size) and method structure. PGS004535 reports a materially stronger OR (1.6007) than PGS004465 (1.3496), crossing the typical ‘strong’ OR≈1.5 threshold, making it more likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark when explicit AUC/R2 are absent. Additionally, its RFDiseasemetaPRS method suggests multi-score/meta-PRS aggregation, which is a positive structural signal versus a single-score LDpred2 build when endpoints and cohorts are otherwise the same. Strongest runner-up: PGS004465, which uses LDpred2 (a strong genome-wide shrinkage method), but its weaker OR makes it less likely to be the top performer in the hidden benchmark given the near-clone context.

Direct-match cluster for target_trait kidney failure is primarily the kidney-failure EFO candidates: PGS000708 (Kidney failure; phenotyping: diabetic kidney failure), plus the ICD-coded chronic renal failure/kidney failure models PGS004562 and PGS004492 (N18 chronic renal failure). Exclude clearly off-trait acute kidney injury models (PGS004491, PGS004561) and CKD/eGFR-proxy or CKD-stage models as less endpoint-faithful to ‘kidney failure’. Among the direct-match set, PGS000708 is best-supported for likely #1 external benchmark performance because it provides the strongest comparable discrimination evidence (C-index 0.779 in EUR evaluation, large eval n=135,300) alongside a solid per-SD HR=1.19, using a modern high-dimensional snpnet approach with substantial variant count (183,272). The strongest runner-up is PGS004562, which matches kidney failure via N18 chronic renal failure and has a large training set (n=174,489) and high OR=1.395, but it lacks any reported AUC/C-index/R² and has unknown covariates, making its apparent strength less benchmark-predictive than PGS000708’s explicit discrimination metric in a large evaluation.

Direct-match cluster is the lymphoid-leukemia/CLL scores (PGS000649/651/646/647/650/648/874/2305/003453; plus broader lymphocytic/lymphoid leukemia PGS000077/000788/000645). Excluding PGS003448 because its trait_reported is acute lymphoblastic leukemia and its effect size is ~null (OR 0.95), making it off-target/weak despite a CLL phenotyping string.

Among the coherent CLL candidates, PGS003453 is most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark because it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=2.17, 95% CI 2.07–2.28) on a clean, direct CLL endpoint with large European evaluation (n=20,134), suggesting robust PRS signal without relying on covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. This is stronger and more stable evidence of PRS discrimination than the PRSweb siblings’ modest full-model AUROCs (~0.67–0.70) from small evaluations.

Strongest runner-up: PGS000874, which shows a very high C-index (0.861) and large top-vs-rest OR (3.79), but its phenotyping is restricted to individuals with a family history of hematological cancers (selection/packaging risk for general-population benchmarking) and has much smaller validation (n=3,958). PGS003453 is more likely to transfer as the top benchmark performer because it targets general CLL without the family-history restriction and has a stronger, tightly estimated per-SD OR in a larger evaluation.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches for osteoporosis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so the decision hinges on transferable PRS signal evidence. The strongest same-study cluster is the 2024 Commun Biol ‘risk factor metaPRS’ family (PGS004565/PGS004560/PGS004495/PGS004490), where the RFDiseasemetaPRS models show materially higher per-SD effect sizes than the LDpred2 siblings. Within that cluster, PGS004565 has the highest reported OR (1.328) with the same EUR→EUR context and identical validation size (n=56,192), making it the best bet to rank #1 in an external benchmark. Strongest runner-up is PGS004560 (OR 1.321) from the same method/publication/endpoint family, but it is slightly weaker on the only comparable performance signal available (effect size).

Both candidates are direct matches to otosclerosis, but PGS001255 has the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.6319 and PGS-only R²=0.01341 (with full-model AUROC=0.6532), giving a concrete, standalone discrimination signal that is plausibly below the local h2_obs ceiling and therefore interpretable. The strongest runner-up is PGS002046, which has a method/structure advantage (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 570k variants) but only reports a very small partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182) and lacks PRS-only AUROC/R², making its expected benchmark ranking more uncertain despite the larger variant set.

PGS005217 is the strongest direct-match for peripheral vascular disease because it targets the closest clinical entity (peripheral artery disease / peripheral arterial disease) with high endpoint fidelity (incident PAD), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant coverage (~1.3M), and shows strong PRS signal via effect size (HR per SD 1.66) alongside broad multi-ancestry evaluation. The strongest runner-up is PGS002055 (same portability-paper family as PGS001843) because it is an exact-label match to ‘peripheral vascular disease’ and uses LDpred2 with many variants, but its evidence is limited to a weak partial correlation (0.0175) from a UKB portability framework context with no effect-size or PRS-comparable discrimination metrics, making it less likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark than the disease-focused PAD model with strong HR evidence.

Direct-match cluster for target trait (nodular goiter) is the three "Benign nodular goiter" models from the same disease-focused multi-biobank study (PGS005261/PGS005262/PGS005263). The two "thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter" candidates (PGS005273/PGS005274) are off-target because they model malignancy-vs-benign differential diagnosis rather than nodular goiter risk, and the UKB portability scores for "nontoxic multinodular goiter" (PGS001814/PGS002022) are framework-style with weak PRS signal (partial-r ~0.025–0.028) and narrower validation context.

Within the benign nodular goiter sibling set, PGS005262 is most likely to rank #1 externally because it combines a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.085M variants) with the strongest reported effect-size evidence among the benign-goiter models (OR per SD 1.41 vs 1.36 for PGS005263 and 1.05 for the sparse P+T PGS005261). Full-model AUROC differences are small and not decisive, but they are at least consistent with PGS005262 being the strongest PRS-driven model in this same-endpoint, same-validation setting.

Strongest runner-up: PGS005263 (same endpoint and method family, similar variant count), but it has a weaker OR (1.36 vs 1.41) and slightly lower full-model AUROC (0.588 vs 0.593), making PGS005262 the better bet for top hidden-benchmark performance.

Both candidates are direct matches to psoriatic arthritis (PGS000342 explicitly; PGS001287 uses the near-synonym psoriatic arthropathy with trait_efo=psoriatic arthritis). PGS001287 is more likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark because it provides strong PRS-comparable performance evidence (PGS-only AUROC=0.676 and PGS R²(no covariates)=0.0335, with full-model AUROC=0.728 using only basic covariates), and it is trained/evaluated in a large, well-characterized UKB setting. The strongest runner-up is PGS000342, which has excellent endpoint fidelity and disease-focused framing, but it reports only a modest full-model AUROC=0.562 with unknown covariates and no PRS-only metrics, making its standalone PRS signal and benchmark transferability much less supported.

Direct-match cluster is the set with trait_efo = ovarian neoplasm / ovarian carcinoma and phenotyping_reported indicating ovarian cancer/neoplasm diagnosis (excluding clear special-population BRCA-carrier scores and interaction/packaging endpoints). Within the largest coherent same-endpoint sibling family (Cancer PRSweb: malignant neoplasm of ovary; EUR; basic covariates age/sex/PCs/batch), PGS000550 (PRS-CS) has the strongest visible PRS signal: highest full-model AUROC among those siblings (0.568) and the highest reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.286) plus the highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0113), making it the best-supported pick for external ranking within that like-for-like context. Strongest runner-up is PGS000549 (GWAS Hits), which has nearly comparable AUROC (0.567) but materially weaker effect size (OR=1.263) and lower pseudo-R² (0.00996); given identical endpoint/covariates/ancestry and same study family, those differences favor PGS000550 as more likely to rank #1 in a hidden benchmark.

PGS000903 is the strongest direct-match Parkinson disease risk PRS in the shortlist because it comes from a large, disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis context (same Lancet Neurol study family as PGS000902), uses a more polygenic construction (C+T with 1,805 variants vs 90 GWAS hits), and is the only candidate here with a reasonably PRS-informative quantitative signal beyond a covariate-heavy full-model AUROC—reporting both an R² (0.054) and a strong case-control separation (OR 6.25 for top vs bottom quartile). The strongest runner-up is PGS000902 (same study family, same endpoint/covariates, similar validation N), but it is a much sparser 90-variant GWAS-hits score and shows weaker discrimination evidence (lower AUROC 0.651 and no comparable R²/OR shown), making it less likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches to pancreatic carcinoma via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma, with PGS002264 (pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) also a plausible dominant-subtype match but with heavier clinical packaging. Among the cleanest, most benchmark-transferable PRS candidates, PGS000083 and PGS000794 are near-clones: both are 22 genome-wide significant variants, same incident pancreatic cancer endpoint, same covariate set (demographics/PCs plus standard exposures and family history), same evaluation ancestry (EUR), same validation size (n=391,491), and essentially identical reported discrimination (AUROC ~0.745; HR per SD ~1.49). In this tie, PGS000083 is more likely to rank #1 because it is the base, directly specified genome-wide-significant PRS with coherent reporting, whereas PGS000794 is explicitly a derivative reweighting (“inverse variant weights”) of PGS000083, which adds transformation/implementation risk without any visible performance gain. Strongest runner-up: PGS000794, because it matches the same endpoint/study context and metrics, but is slightly less well-supported due to being a modified-weight variant with no demonstrated advantage.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for obesity, but several are penalized as framework/portability (PGS001825, PGS002033) or pan-trait sparse (PGS001298), while others lack PRS-comparable metrics and provide only effect sizes (PGS005235, PGS004447, PGS004517, PGS005145, PGS005154) or are BMI/ad hoc GWAS-hit constructions with unclear PRS-only evaluation (PGS003400, PGS003959). Within the strongest direct-match cluster with PRS-comparable evidence, PGS002033 (LDpred2) is the clear leader because it reports a higher PRS-only metric (partial correlation 0.0789 in EUR validation) than its same-publication near-clone PGS001825 (penalized regression partial-r 0.0547), with identical endpoint framing and covariates, making this a strong within-context tie-break. The strongest runner-up is PGS005235 (LDpred2-auto; obesity phecode endpoint; OR≈1.97), which has an impressive effect size and large EUR evaluation, but the absence of PRS-only AUC/R2 (and reliance on a single OR without comparable discrimination metrics) makes it less reliably benchmark-dominant than PGS002033’s directly comparable PRS-only performance signal.

PGS004530 is the strongest direct-match pulmonary embolism candidate because it targets the exact ICD10 endpoint (I26) with coherent phenotype alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all pulmonary embolism) and uses an ensemble-style method (RFDiseasemetaPRS) that structurally tends to outperform single-score constructions in external benchmarks. Despite missing PRS-comparable AUC/R2, it provides the strongest available per-SD effect size signal among the exact-endpoint siblings (OR=1.242 vs 1.167 for PGS004460) in the same evaluation context (EUR, same UKB-based training and same validation size), making it the best-supported pick for #1 hidden benchmark performance. Strongest runner-up: PGS004460, which is the same exact endpoint and study family with a solid genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) but has a materially weaker reported OR in the same context, so it is less likely to top the benchmark.

PGS003586 is the cleanest direct-match for the target trait (trait_reported and trait_efo both preeclampsia, with phenotyping_reported explicitly pre-eclampsia/eclampsia) and comes from the disease-focused Nat Med study family. Within the same-context sibling pair from that paper (PGS003586 vs PGS003587), endpoints/covariates/validation setting are essentially identical, so the stronger per-SD effect size is the key tie-break: OR 1.31 (1.24–1.38) for PGS003586 vs OR 1.20 (1.14–1.26) for PGS003587, making PGS003586 more likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark. The strongest runner-up is PGS003587 because it shares the same study family and phenotype ascertainment, but its weaker OR suggests lower standalone PRS signal. PGS004593 is deprioritized despite large validation N because its phenotyping_reported is gestational hypertension (endpoint mismatch for a preeclampsia benchmark) and it reports an HR in a different modeling context, making cross-model comparability weaker.

Within the direct-match rheumatoid arthritis cluster, PGS004163 is the strongest-supported for a generic RA benchmark because it has high endpoint fidelity (seropositive RA, a coherent RA diagnosis subtype), clean comparability (covariates listed as 0, reducing risk that performance is covariate-driven), and the best visible discrimination/effect evidence among the same-study near-clones: full-model AUROC 0.7469 with the highest reported R² (0.1376) and the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 2.46) in that coherent 2023 multi-method RA evaluation family. The strongest runner-up is PGS004049 (LDpred2.CV), which is very close but has slightly weaker effect size (OR 2.37) and lower R² (0.1220) in the same endpoint/validation context, making PGS004163 the more likely #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

All four candidates are broadly on-trait for sarcoidosis, but PGS001872 and PGS002084 have a trait_efo of "skin sarcoidosis" (a narrower/possibly mismapped subtype) and only report partial correlation (no PRS-comparable AUROC/R²), making them less directly supported for a generic sarcoidosis benchmark despite stronger method/variant-count structure. Between the two exact sarcoidosis EFO snpnet siblings (PGS000923 vs PGS000922) from the same pan-trait UKB framework context with identical covariates and validation setting, PGS000923 has consistently slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.6456 vs 0.6428; PGS-only R² 0.0180 vs 0.0174; full-model AUROC 0.6546 vs 0.6486), so it is the best-supported direct-match pick. Strongest runner-up: PGS000922, which is nearly identical but marginally weaker on the comparable PRS-only metrics.

Direct-match cluster for psoriasis includes PGS001312/PGS001313/PGS001871/PGS002083/PGS002293/PGS002344/PGS002465/PGS002514/PGS002612/PGS002416/PGS002563/PGS002661/PGS002710 plus the newer severe-psoriasis scores (PGS005307/PGS005308/PGS005309/PGS005310) and the Newfoundland severity/genital-area subphenotypes (PGS004315/PGS004316/PGS004317). Excluding off-trait psoriatic arthritis models (PGS001287, PGS000342) and down-weighting subtype-only endpoints (severe psoriasis; genital-area; severity-only) for a generic psoriasis benchmark, PGS001312 is best-supported because it is an exact psoriasis endpoint with explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6916; PGS-only R²=0.0523) and strong incremental AUROC (0.145) under standard covariates, giving the clearest evidence of standalone PRS signal among the direct-match candidates. Strongest runner-up is PGS001871 (same UKB portability context, partial-r=0.0636), but partial-r is less directly comparable/diagnostic than PGS-only AUROC/R² and does not show a clearer advantage; other contenders either lack PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS005309/PGS005310 report ORs but are severe-psoriasis endpoints) or show near-zero incremental R² in the Nat Genet cross-population set (e.g., PGS002344/PGS002661).

Direct-match cluster is the PRS-CS schizophrenia diagnosis endpoints from the Am J Psychiatry multi-health-system study (PGS000133/134/135/136); PGS002785 is excluded as off-trait because its phenotyping_reported is cognitive function rather than schizophrenia. Within the direct-match siblings, PGS000136 has the strongest combined visible performance evidence that is least likely to be a pure small-sample artifact: it shows higher full-model AUROC (0.64, 95% CI 0.60–0.69) plus a strong per-SD OR (1.7) on a reasonably sized EUR validation (n=18,461) with only basic covariates. Strongest runner-up is PGS000135, which reports a higher AUROC (0.74) but on a much smaller validation sample (n=9,569) and without supporting effect-size evidence, making it more likely to be an optimistic/unstable estimate relative to the more corroborated signal in PGS000136.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for prostate cancer, but several are endpoint-packaged (e.g., 5-year incident absolute-risk wrappers) or subtype/phase-specific (lethal/fatal/aggressive), which reduces direct comparability for a generic “prostate cancer” benchmark. Within the cleanest direct-diagnosis cluster, PGS000584 (PRS-CS; 1,120,596 variants; EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL) has the strongest internally consistent PRS signal among the PRSweb-style models: highest full-model AUROC (0.705) in that family with basic covariates only (age/sex/PCs/batch), plus strong effect-size evidence (OR per SD 2.173) and top-1% vs rest OR 5.58, suggesting robust discrimination not reliant on heavy clinical covariates. The strongest runner-up is PGS000588 (lassosum; 178,259 variants; AUROC 0.699; OR per SD 2.127; top-1% OR 5.88), which is very close but slightly weaker on AUROC and per-SD OR while also using a less genome-wide shrinkage approach than PRS-CS; given near-identical endpoint/covariates/context, those small but consistent advantages favor PGS000584 as most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark.

All shortlisted candidates have missing visible metadata (no trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, no performance metrics, no method, no ancestry, no covariates), so endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance cannot be assessed and no direct-match cluster can be formed. Under this complete-information tie, the only admissible choice is effectively arbitrary among the provided IDs; I select PGS000598. Strongest runner-up: PGS000599, which is indistinguishable from the winner given the fully missing records.

All four candidates are direct matches to retinal detachment, but PGS001137 is the best-supported because it reports explicit PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC=0.573 and PGS-only R2=0.00663 in European validation) with basic covariates, giving the clearest evidence of standalone genetic signal and transfer potential. The strongest runner-up is PGS002040: it has a stronger method/structure signal (LDpred2 with genome-wide variant count) and a higher partial correlation (0.0276 vs 0.0218 for PGS001833), but it lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2, making its advantage less benchmark-predictive than PGS001137’s directly comparable PRS-only metrics. PGS000990 is slightly off-endpoint (time-to-event retinal detachments and breaks) and has weaker PRS-only metrics than PGS001137.

All three are plausible direct matches (pulmonary fibrosis / idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis), but PGS001791 is most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark because it is a genome-wide PRS (PRS-CS-auto; 910,439 variants) with an explicit PRS-comparable metric in EUR (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.005929), which is the cleanest available signal of standalone PRS contribution among the shortlist. The strongest runner-up is PGS004695: it has excellent endpoint fidelity (incident idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) and a strong risk-gradient effect size (HR 3.78 high vs low quintile) in a very large EUR evaluation, but it is a 23-SNP genome-wide-significant score and provides no PRS-only AUC/R2, making it less reliably predictive of top benchmark discrimination than a genome-wide shrinkage PRS with explicit PRS-only R2 evidence. PGS001030 is penalized as a pan-trait UKB sparse-framework score (snpnet, 51 variants) despite reporting PGS-only AUROC/R2, which tends to transfer less well than disease-targeted/multi-biobank genome-wide PRS approaches.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to carcinoma in situ of skin) and share the same publication family, ancestry context (EUR throughout), covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), training cohort (MGI), and validation size (n=5,500), so the best predictor of hidden-benchmark rank is the within-family empirical performance/effect-size signal. PGS000471 (lassosum) has the strongest reported discrimination and PRS signal among the siblings: highest full-model AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557/0.524), highest Nagelkerke R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154/0.00141), strongest per-SD OR (1.401 vs 1.308/1.09), and strongest top-1% vs rest OR (3.77 vs 2.45/1.48). The strongest runner-up is PGS000470, which is clearly better than PGS000469 but is consistently weaker than PGS000471 on AUROC, pseudo-R², and effect sizes; PGS000469 also underperforms substantially despite using PRS-CS, suggesting its fitted score is weaker in this endpoint/context.
