Direct-match cluster includes generic sleep apnea and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) models; OSA is a clinically dominant subtype and is endpoint-faithful here (phenotyping_reported: obstructive sleep apnea). Among the OSA candidates, PGS005219 has the strongest PRS-discrimination evidence via effect size (OR per SD=1.98, 95% CI 1.74–2.24) and uses a structurally strong approach (weighted multi-score summation of PRS-CS components with ~983k variants) developed across multiple large cohorts (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) with multi-ancestry evaluation, which is more predictive of external benchmark rank than the ExPRSweb framework scores whose full-model AUROCs hover ~0.49–0.53 and show weak/near-null ORs. Strongest runner-up is PGS005220 (same study/method/endpoint family and same AUROC=0.79) but it has materially weaker effect size (OR=1.53 vs 1.98), making PGS005219 the more likely #1 in a hidden same-trait performance benchmark.

Direct-match cluster is the set with trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all = squamous cell carcinoma (PGS000467, PGS000460, PGS000120, PGS000464, PGS000465, PGS000461, PGS000731, PGS000463, PGS000466, PGS000468, PGS000462). Excluded as off-trait/special-population: esophageal cancer models (PGS000363/4/5/6) and site-specific SCC subtypes (lung/head&neck) plus the childhood-cancer-survivor SCC risk model (PGS005209) due to restricted endpoint/covariate context.

Within the direct SCC cluster, PGS000461 has the strongest overall performance evidence in a comparable, PRS-light setting: it shows the highest full-model AUROC among the PRSweb SCC siblings (0.599) and the strongest accompanying effect size (OR per SD 1.491) with the top pseudo-R² in that same sibling set (0.0304), all under basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs) and a clean SCC diagnosis phenotype. This combination is the best visible predictor of ranking #1 in an external same-trait benchmark when no PGS-only AUC/R² is available.

Strongest runner-up: PGS000731, which reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.605) and large validation N, but has unknown covariates and lacks supporting PRS-specific metrics beyond a modest per-SD OR (1.44); that makes its apparent AUROC edge less reliable/comparable than PGS000461’s cleaner covariate disclosure and stronger effect-size/R² package.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches for urinary bladder cancer (trait_reported and trait_efo align; phenotyping_reported is bladder cancer/incident bladder cancer/urothelial carcinoma). Within the strongest same-trait cluster (Cancer PRSweb bladder cancer models with comparable EUR-only context and similar covariates), PGS000613 has the best overall PRS signal: highest per-SD effect size (OR=1.301, 95% CI 1.227–1.379) and the strongest tail separation (OR top 1% vs rest = 2.91, 95% CI 1.99–4.24), with similar full-model AUROC (~0.571) to its siblings. The strongest runner-up is PGS000610 (near-clone PRSweb model with similar covariates and AUROC=0.572), but it has weaker effect sizes (OR=1.292; top 1% OR=1.47 with wide CI), making it less likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark where PRS-driven discrimination (not covariate-driven full-model AUROC) is decisive.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for thyroid carcinoma/cancer, but several are endpoint-restricted or packaged in ways that reduce comparability (e.g., childhood-cancer-survivor subsequent thyroid cancer: PGS001354/PGS005210; thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter: PGS005273/PGS005274). Among the direct disease-endpoint candidates, PGS005259 is the strongest overall evidence package for likely #1 external benchmark performance: it is a genome-wide PRSCS model (~1.09M variants; structurally strong for capturing polygenic signal), developed/validated in a large, explicitly disease-focused global multi-ancestry study spanning many biobanks, and it shows the strongest visible per-SD effect size in the pool (OR≈2.04; β≈0.71) alongside a competitive AUROC (~0.695) in a multi-ancestry evaluation context—signals consistent with robust transferable discrimination. The strongest runner-up is PGS000797 (incident thyroid cancer; HR=1.75; very large validation n≈391k), but it is a small 12-variant score (and even described as derived from another score with inverse weights), making it less likely to outperform a well-powered genome-wide PRSCS model in a hidden benchmark focused on PRS performance.

Direct-match cluster includes all five (urolithiasis / urinary calculus / calculus of kidney and ureter / nephrolithiasis are all on-target). Among them, PGS004563 is most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark because it comes from a disease-focused integration study archetype and uses an explicit meta/ensemble-style construction (RFDiseasemetaPRS), which is a strong structural predictor of better transfer when head-to-head metrics are sparse. It also shows the stronger per-SD effect size signal within its near-clone family (OR 1.283 vs 1.227 for sibling PGS004493) on the same endpoint and validation context, making it the best-supported pick inside that coherent study cluster. Strongest runner-up is PGS002075 (LDpred2 portability score) because it has a PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0385) and a strong genome-wide method, but it is from a UKB portability/framework setting and lacks richer disease-focused performance evidence; that combination is less predictive of top external-benchmark rank than the disease-focused metaPRS with the stronger effect size among its siblings.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly direct matches on trait_efo (type 1 diabetes mellitus), but several are endpoint-mismatched or packaged (e.g., PGS000869 is cystic-fibrosis related diabetes; PGS003749 restricts to age at diagnosis <25; PGS001296 is time-to-event insulin-dependent diabetes). Within the strongest coherent direct-match cluster (the 2023 Am J Hum Genet five-biobank evaluation family with phenotyping_reported=T1D and covariates=0), PGS004162 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the best within-family performance signals: highest full-model AUROC (0.771) and highest R² (0.141) plus the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 2.89, β 1.06) among its same-context siblings, making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark. The strongest runner-up is PGS004874 (Nat Commun incidence framework; C-index 0.77, HR 2.37, very large eval N), but it is incident time-to-event with different metric type and covariate adjustment (PCs 1–10) and lacks comparable PRS-only metrics; given near-identical headline discrimination but weaker comparability, it is slightly less likely than the top-performing MultiPRS sibling to be the benchmark #1.

All shortlisted candidates are direct matches on trait_efo/phenotyping except PGS001307, which is explicitly time-to-event (a mild endpoint mismatch for generic ulcerative colitis risk). Among the remaining direct case/control-style UC scores, PGS001306 has the strongest PRS-comparable evidence: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.630) and PGS-only R² (0.0204), plus a higher full-model AUROC (0.662) than the portability-framework alternatives. The strongest runner-up is PGS004253 because it is also a direct UC endpoint and uses a strong genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with very large variant count and a strong per-SD OR (1.84), but its evidence is less benchmark-transferable here because only full-model AUROC is shown (no PGS-only metrics) and it comes from a more context-specific study framing (ICI-mediated colitis) with smaller training/validation than the UKB-wide framework scores. Given the hidden benchmark is same-trait PRS performance, the explicit PGS-only metrics in PGS001306 make it the best-supported pick.

Direct-match cluster for target uterine cancer includes the uterine/uterus-labeled scores (PGS001795, PGS000541, PGS000542, PGS003740) and the clinically dominant subtype endometrial cancer scores (e.g., PGS003381, PGS000075, PGS000786, etc.). Among the uterus-labeled direct matches, PGS001795 is most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark because it combines (i) exact endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: uterine cancer), (ii) a methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto; 911,692 variants) that should capture more polygenic signal than the very sparse PRSweb GWAS-hits/P+T uterus scores (18–20 variants), and (iii) the only explicitly PRS-comparable metric in the uterus-labeled set (PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.001948), which is plausible under the provided low heritability ceiling and indicates nontrivial standalone PRS signal. Strongest runner-up is PGS000541 (Malignant neoplasm of uterus; GWAS hits; AUROC 0.576 with basic covariates), but it is structurally much sparser and its modest full-model AUROC advantage over PGS000542 is not compelling evidence of better PRS transfer; it also lacks any PRS-only metric, making it less predictive of benchmark ranking than PGS001795.

Direct-match clustering by endpoint fidelity excludes two candidates as clearly off-target for generic vitiligo risk: PGS000760 is evaluated on treatment-induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients (anti–PD-L1 induced), and PGS001536 is a UKB pan-trait framework score with a time-to-event vitiligo endpoint (TTE), which is a weaker match for a generic vitiligo target and carries the known framework/portability penalty. PGS000738 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo are vitiligo and whose study context is vitiligo-focused polygenic inheritance; it also shows a substantial per-SD effect size (β≈0.695) with a nontrivial pseudo-R² (~0.039) in EUR evaluation, consistent with being a meaningful PRS signal and well below the vitiligo heritability ceiling. Strongest runner-up is PGS001536 because it reports explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², but its pan-trait snpnet origin plus TTE endpoint makes it less likely to rank #1 in an external same-trait benchmark than the disease-focused, endpoint-faithful PGS000738.

All shortlisted candidates are broadly on-trait for type 2 diabetes, but many are either (i) framework/portability repositories (e.g., ExPRSweb), (ii) subtype/restricted endpoints (e.g., prediabetics-only, glucocorticoid-induced hyperglycemia), or (iii) heavily covariate-inflated full-model AUROCs that are not PRS-comparable. PGS002308 is a clean direct T2D diagnosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Type 2 diabetes) with a strong, modern genome-wide method (PRS-CSx; 1.26M variants) and unusually informative PRS-relevant evidence: high per-SD effect size (OR=1.96) plus an explicit R²=0.092, which is strong and plausibly below the provided liability h² ceiling (~0.219). It is also explicitly designed as a trans-ancestry PRS and validated in a large sample (n=54,793), improving expected external benchmark transfer.

Strongest runner-up: PGS003114 (lassosum; incident T2D; AUROC=0.825; OR=3.959; UKB-based). Despite its very strong-looking AUROC/OR, it comes from an ExPRSweb-style repository context and reports only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics; the very large OR alongside a high AUROC raises concern that the reported discrimination is not directly comparable/portable. PGS002308’s combination of endpoint fidelity, trans-ancestry design, and the presence of an explicit R² signal makes it more likely to rank #1 in a hidden external same-trait benchmark.
